uncited: Parametric Function Generation constructs transfer functions by evaluating mathematical functions of a normalized scalar input to determine color and opacity values, rather than relying on piecewise linear interpolation between user-defined control points.

It differs from sibling methods like [Voxel Color Mapping](2970-voxel-color-mapping.md) and [Color Specification](3969-color-specification.md) by defining the mapping through continuous analytical formulas (e.g., Gaussians, sigmoids, or trigonometric functions) rather than explicit lookup table entries or discrete color specifications.
The family shares the mechanism of mapping a normalized scalar input $t \in [0, 1]$ to an RGBA output vector $\mathbf{C}$ using a parametric equation.
The input $t$ is typically derived from the parent method [1D Transfer Function Generation and Sampling](2689-1d-transfer-function-generation-and-sampling.md), which normalizes raw voxel values.
The output is a 4-channel vector where the first three channels represent RGB color and the fourth represents alpha (opacity).
The specific parametric form varies by child method, but the core operation is the evaluation of a function $f(t)$ that yields $\mathbf{C}$.
The concept of parametric transfer functions allows for smooth, continuous mapping of scalar data to visual properties, avoiding the jagged edges of piecewise linear interpolation.
